solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American, say, has zero chance to lose face

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: to lose face means the word for chance drops its front letter, its face

parts.note: chance as an adjective means accidental, happening by luck

explanation.surface: An American is said to have no chance at all of being humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose face' removes the front letter of the word for chance.
explanation.definitionFit: An Occidental is a Westerner, and an American is one example of a person from the West.

clue.text: Excessive love for extract of roses

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, excessive
love is zero in tennis scoring, O

explanation.surface: Too much affection is shown towards rose essence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' looks romantic, but it is the tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto, or attar, is the fragrant oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Mixed school member welcoming Eton's Head

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: a school is a shoal of fish, and a cod is one member of it

indicators.note: Head means the first letter, the top of Eton

explanation.surface: A pupil at a mixed school greets the headmaster of Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks educational but means a group of fish; 'welcoming' puts E inside COD.
explanation.definitionFit: Coed is an adjective for education of both sexes together, so a coed school is mixed.

clue.text: Thought opera composer wants second helping

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Léo Delibes was a French composer of the opera Lakmé
a ration is a portion, a helping of food

explanation.surface: A composer of opera thinks about having a second plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means lacks: DELIBES without S gives DELIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation is careful consideration, the act of thinking something through.

clue.text: Most of the alcohol knocked back? Time for bed

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters are turned round, read backwards, as well as a drink downed
most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: the word the, written out
gin is a kind of alcohol

explanation.surface: After downing most of the drink, it is time to go to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts THE to TH, and 'knocked back' reverses THGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time when people normally go to sleep.

clue.text: Guerrilla supporting a wild naval barrage

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed underneath, so the guerrilla comes last
wild means out of control, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Che Guevara was the famous Argentine guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: A guerrilla backs a frenzied naval bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns NAVAL into VALAN; 'supporting' puts CHE below.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is an overwhelming flood of things, like a barrage of questions.

clue.text: What may, paradoxically, be evens?

parts.note: in betting, evens is a price, and prices are called by a word that is the opposite of even numbers

explanation.surface: A riddle about how something called by one name could be its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Betting prices are 'odds', and evens (one-to-one) is one such price, so the odds can be evens.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is a betting price, and betting prices in general are known by the opposite of even.

clue.text: Inconstancy of underworld rulers switching sides

indicators.note: switching sides means right changes to left, one abbreviation for the other

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
royalty means monarchs, rulers

explanation.surface: Kings of the underworld defect and show their fickleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching sides' replaces R (right) with L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Disloyalty is a failure to remain faithful, which is a form of fickleness.

clue.text: Bound to precede current period of the year

indicators.note: to precede means the word for bound comes before the word for current

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring
a tide is a current of water

explanation.surface: Something is sure to come before the present season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain' and 'current' like 'present'; they are a leap and a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Springtide is an old poetic word for springtime, a season.

clue.text: Scholar thus comprehending old sayings of Christ

indicators.note: comprehending means taking in, so one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: thus in the sense of therefore can be then
logia are the collected sayings attributed to Jesus

explanation.surface: A scholar is shown grasping ancient words attributed to Jesus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' here is the logical 'therefore', and 'comprehending' means containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologian is an academic who studies religion, a kind of learned specialist.

clue.text: Emperor of eastern half of Sikh city

indicators.note: in an across entry east is the right-hand side, so the back four letters of the city are kept

parts.note: Amritsar in Punjab is home to the Golden Temple, the holiest Sikh shrine

explanation.surface: A ruler is said to govern the eastern part of a city sacred to Sikhs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern half of' keeps the right-hand half of AMRITSAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the hereditary ruler of Russia, with the title of emperor.

clue.text: I'm surprised to settle after industrial action

indicators.note: after means the word for settle comes behind

parts.note: a strike is a walkout, industrial action
alight means land, settle like a bird

explanation.surface: Someone expresses surprise at agreeing terms after a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike a light!' is an old British exclamation of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dated British exclamation of shock, roughly 'goodness me!'

clue.text: Marshal bans turncoat for malice or deceit, say

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official forbids a traitor because of his spite or duplicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like a title, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange BANS TURNCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice and deceit are nouns naming qualities rather than things, which is what grammarians call this kind of noun.

clue.text: This entertains upper-class rogue in depression

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for depression

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
a devil is a rascal, a rogue

explanation.surface: A posh scoundrel feeling down provides some entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low spirits but means a dip in the land; U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville is variety theatre, a form of popular show meant to amuse audiences.

clue.text: Failing to store pounds up, dourer retiring person

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, reversed
to store means to hold inside, so the pound sign goes within

parts.note: a failing is a flaw
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra
lower, as in to lour or frown, gives a comparative meaning more sullen

explanation.surface: A gloomy, shy person fails to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to store' puts L in FLAW (FLLAW), which 'up' reverses to WALLF.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is a shy person who stays at the side at a party, someone retiring.

clue.text: Like e.g. sprinting writer after running on area

indicators.note: after means the pen comes behind the shuffled letters
running means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A writer is shown jogging across a patch of ground, as in a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' signals the anagram; Bic is a common ballpoint brand, so the 'writer' is a pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprinting is anaerobic exercise: short bursts where muscles work without enough oxygen.

clue.text: Brief exchange about teacher from the south

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word surrounds the other

parts.note: to barter is to exchange goods

indicators.note: from the south in a down clue means reading upwards, reversed

parts.note: sir is what British pupils call a male teacher

explanation.surface: A short swap of views about a teacher who comes from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' reverses SIR to RIS; 'about' puts RIS in BARTER. 'Brief' seems an adjective but is the slang noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief is British slang for a lawyer, especially a barrister handling a case.

clue.text: Not becoming trendy, a parent's gutted

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, so only the outside letters of parent stay

explanation.surface: Someone's mother or father is devastated at not looking fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' empties PARENT to PT, and the 's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable, and becoming here means fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: Pottery, fifty artful bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, as a bottle holds liquid

parts.note: artful means skilful, deft
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty skilfully made pots are being bottled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' puts L inside DEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware named after the Dutch town where it was made.

clue.text: Staggered about European Court sitting again

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word wraps around the others

parts.note: staggered means reeled, walked unsteadily

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled around a European court that was in session once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the word for staggered round the two abbreviations; 'sitting' is the parliamentary sense of holding a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A re-elected member is returned to office and so is again holding their seat in a parliament.

clue.text: Can spinning coppers turn everything red?

indicators.note: spinning means turned round, so the word for can is read backwards

parts.note: can is slang for a lavatory, a lav
coppers is slang for the police

indicators.note: turn means the word for everything is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A question whether whirling police officers can make the whole lot go red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' turns LAV into VAL and 'turn' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valpolicella is a red wine from the Veneto region of Italy, and red is short for red wine.

clue.text: Girl: in Paris, she's given name

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A French girl is given her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a female first name, so a girl's name stands for a girl.

clue.text: What's essential to distinguish, in this clue

indicators.note: what is essential to the words is what lies in their core, so the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: A question about what matters most in telling things apart in this clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sits within 'distinguisH IN This', and the definition is the last word of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a suggestion that helps someone find an answer, like a crossword clue.

clue.text: Chap's going to the pit

definitions.meaning: read as a contraction, the chap will
the pit is a traditional name for ..., the abyss

explanation.surface: A man is heading off to the mine.
explanation.definitionFit: He'll is the contraction for 'he will', and the bottomless pit is the place of the damned.

clue.text: Fabric which is green and needs cutting

definitions.meaning: a fine linen or cotton cloth
a stretch of grass that has to be mown

explanation.surface: A cloth that is green and has to be trimmed to size.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is a fine sheer linen, and a lawn is also mown grass in a garden.

clue.text: One seen in cave is a little bit camp, at first

indicators.note: at first means the camp word comes in front

parts.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
a mite is a tiny amount, a little bit

explanation.surface: Something found in a cavern is said to be slightly camp at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' looks like the adjective for flamboyant, but it is a noun, a prison camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite is a mineral column rising from a cave floor.

clue.text: Rake in vase, so we're told

indicators.note: so we're told signals a word heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: Someone is told to gather leaves into a vase.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike in a non-rhotic (British) accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake in money is an idiom for earning a lot of it.

clue.text: Final reckoning with child, a learner on piano

indicators.note: on in an across clue means following, so the piano comes first

parts.note: a grand is a kind of piano
a tot is a small child
L is for learner, as on British learner drivers' plates

explanation.surface: A last tally of a child and a pupil sitting at the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue means coming after, so the piano word goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand total is the overall sum at the end of a calculation, the final tally.
